The Supreme Court analyzed the distinction between fraudulent misrepresentation and the penal offence of forgery under Section 467 and Section 468 of the Indian Penal Code.

The Bench reiterated that to constitute forgery under Section 463 and Section 464 IPC, the document must be a false document made with intent to cause damage or injury. A document containing false assertions of fact is not a false document if it is signed by the person who purports to sign it.

Accordingly, the charges framed under Section 467 and Section 468 IPC are quashed and set aside.
